classification.difficultyReason: Combine a right-triangle relationship and two speeds to minimise a travel-time function with a radical.

inlines.text: Sophie needs to get from point A to point B across a wide river.
The river is 20 m wide, and B is 80 m horizontally from A.
She swims across the river at a speed of 7 km/h and runs at 11 km/h.
that will minimise her total travel time. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: Parallel banks, A on the upper bank, B farther right on the lower bank and a diagonal swimming segment x to a landing point before B. The vertical dimension is 20 m; the complete horizontal displacement from A to B is 80 m. Source blue lines are ordinary geometry and use house black.
spec.mathematics: Swimming distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle of height 20 m; running distance is 80 m minus its horizontal leg.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question diagram; no landing distance or solution supplied.

answer.worked:
Let $y$ m be the horizontal distance from directly opposite A to the landing point. Then $x^2=20^2+y^2$, so $y=\sqrt{x^2-400}$ and the running distance is $80-\sqrt{x^2-400}$ m. Using speeds $7000$ m/h and $11\,000$ m/h,
$$\begin{aligned}T(x)&=\frac{x}{7000}+\frac{80-\sqrt{x^2-400}}{11\,000},\qquad 20\le x\le20\sqrt{17}\\T'(x)&=\frac{1}{7000}-\frac{x}{11\,000\sqrt{x^2-400}}.\end{aligned}$$
At a stationary point,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{7000}&=\frac{x}{11\,000\sqrt{x^2-400}}\\11\sqrt{x^2-400}&=7x\\121(x^2-400)&=49x^2\\72x^2&=48\,400\\x^2&=\frac{6050}{9}\\x&=\frac{55\sqrt2}{3}.\end{aligned}$$
For $x>20$,
$$T''(x)=\frac{400}{11\,000(x^2-400)^{3/2}}>0.$$
Thus $T'$ is increasing and changes from negative to positive at this stationary point, giving the global minimum on the domain. Sophie should swim $\frac{55\sqrt2}{3}\text{ m}\approx25.9\text{ m}$.
